column2: 3.1 Currency and completeness

Is there a pre-defined approach to ensure that metadata is kept up-to-date?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe your approach.
column4: We have a clearly defined metadata approach conform DCAT. So the government organisations can check if the metadata is up to date conform the standard. The datamanagement team of the portal every day checks if the (meta)data is right and if we miss datasets we contact the data owners. Documentation is published for anyone to check how to validate against the Dutch DCAT application profile of DCAT. Currently the DCAT-AP 2 DONL is being created which will implement DCAT AP 2
column7: We have a clearly defined metadata approach conform DCAT. So the government organisations can check if the metadata is up to date conform the standard. The datamanagement team of the portal checks every day to see if the (meta)data is right and if we miss datasets we contact the data owners. Documentation is published for anyone to check how to validate against the Dutch DCAT application profile of DCAT. Currently the DCAT-AP-NL 3.0 is being created, which will implement DCAT-AP 3.

column2:
Do you undertake efforts to ensure that published data covers the full period from when it was first published until today, for example,the complete time series?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please explain the measures in place to ensure complete series of datasets
column7: It is up to the data providers how they would like to present and update their data (multiple entries, or all in one place). For example for this real-time data, downloading the data as CSV-file only shows the last ten timestamps, while it is possible to get all data via an API: https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/22475-real-time-fijnstof-monitoring . For annual datasets, when they are presented as separate datasets, earlier editions can easily be found under 'Related datasets', see this example: https://data.overheid.nl/dataset/monitor-lalo-2015 There are no actions taken to incentivise data providers to provide full time series.

column2: 3.2 Monitoring and measures

Do you monitor the quality of the metadata available on your portal?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly explain how this monitoring takes place. 
* If applicable, please provide the URL to this monitoring mechanism.
column4: We validate at the moment metadata is synced from connected portals. Every dataset must validate against the mandatory setting in our Dutch DCAT application profile. If datasets do not validate, they can't be added to the portal. Responsibility is with the data owner to make sure their metadata validates.

column2:
Do you publish information on the quality of the metadata available on the portal?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please provide the URL to this section.
column4: We check the condition of links to resources every night. In the monitoring statistics results are shown (Quality of the data): https://data.overheid.nl/statistieken/monitor

column2:
Do you publish guidelines (e.g. written materials) and have tools in place, to assist publishers in publishing high-quality metadata? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe this material and (2) provide the URLs to these materials and/or tools.
column7: There is a guideline for publishing data on the portal, including an explanation on the DCAT metadata standard: https://docs.datacommunities.nl/data-overheid-nl-documentatie/datasets-aanmelden/handleiding-datasets-aanmelden-op-data.overheid.nl

column2:
Do you set any standards on metadata quality that data providers must abide by (e.g. on the use of licence, minimum metadata describes, use of certain DCAT-AP properties, etc)

For Explanation:
* If yes, please describe the standards you have in place, i.e. what is minimum information the metadata should describe
column7: The metadata must be conform the Dutch implementation of the DCAT-AP standard.Mandatory field are: title, language, metadata language, description, theme, status, data owner, organisation, license, level of openness, source.

column2:
Do your open data publication/licensing guidelines provide recommendations for the use of Creative Commons (CC) licences, specifically CC BY 4.0 and CC0?

For Explanation:

column7: It is mandatory to select a license, and it is mentioned that the CC-0 license is recommended. On this page the possible licenses are explained: https://data.overheid.nl/ondersteuning/data-publiceren/licentie-keuze

column7: New data providers are always assisted in their data publication process The team is available for support, and there is documentation on the website.

column2: 3.3 DCAT-AP Compliance

Does the national portal follow the DCAT-AP framework or, if not, are standards in place to ensure interoperability with DCAT-AP?

For explanation:
* If the  portal follow the DCAT-AP framework, please describe how compliance with DCAT-AP is ensured
* If the portal does not follow the DCAT-AP framework, please describe how interoperability with DCAT-AP is ensured
column7: Data publishers are required to follow the DCAT-AP-DONL metadata form when they are submitting a dataset. If it not complies, it is not accepted on the portal.

column2: What is the percentage of metadata on your portal that is DCAT-AP compliant, in terms of mandatory classes? (agent, catalogue, dataset, literal, resource)
What is the percentage of metadata on your portal that uses DCAT-AP recommended classes? (category, category scheme, distribution, licence document)
What is the percentage of metadata on your portal that uses DCAT-AP optional classes? (catalogue record, checksum, document, frequency)

Is there a national extension of the DCAT-AP standard developed for your country? 

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly outline the reasons for this decision, and (2) what the main differences between the national variation and the EU standard are.
* If applicable, please provide the URL to the documentation of the national DCAT-AP extension.
column4:
To optimise the searchability and findability of datasets, enrichment of EU standard. There are less free answer options, which enables easier verification of the quality of the metadata. Documentation: https://data.overheid.nl/ondersteuning/open-data/dcat
DCAT 1.1: https://dcat-ap-donl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
DCAT 2.0: https://github.com/dataoverheid/dcat-ap-donl
column7:
To optimise the searchability and findability of datasets, we created a Dutch version as an enrichment of the EU standard. There are less free answer options, which enables easier verification of the quality of the metadata. The latest version (3.0, implementing DCAT-AP 3) is now in consultation:  https://docs.geostandaarden.nl/dcat/dcat-ap-nl30/ Documentation on the standards can be found on the portal: https://data.overheid.nl/ondersteuning/open-data/dcat
DCAT 1.1: https://dcat-ap-donl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
DCAT 2.0: https://github.com/dataoverheid/dcat-ap-donl
